context:
Treat the current SF1 file as a cache-layout compatibility defect, not as
malformed CSV rows: `zstd -t` succeeds for flights/airlines/airports, and a
streaming Python CSV scan reads 25,457,793 data rows with 28 columns and no
malformed rows.

Repair the shared source path by replacing or quarantining the legacy single
large `flights.csv.zst` layout with deterministic FlightData `flights` shards
recorded as multiple manifest entries with explicit CSV dialect metadata.
Keep the fix at the source/manifest contract where practical so DataFusion,
ClickHouse local, DuckDB, and DataFrame loaders resolve the same repaired
table mapping.
description:
FlightData SF 1.0 failed across several SQL and DataFrame platforms during the
UAT sweep. Representative logs include
`datafusion_flightdata_1.0_20260502_182841.log:13`,
`clickhouse-local_flightdata_1.0_20260502_185846.log:15`, and
`polars-df_flightdata_1.0_20260502_211319.log:8`, all pointing at the
`flightdata_1.0/flights.csv.zst` source file being truncated, incomplete, or
otherwise unreadable.

anti_patterns.dont: patch individual adapters to ignore bad rows
anti_patterns.instead: validate or repair the shared source data.
anti_patterns.why: the same corpus failed across engines

preserves.behavior: Existing smaller FlightData scales continue to load.
Reusable datagen corpora stay reusable; cleanup removes run-owned databases, spill directories, and output artifacts, not shared source corpora such as TPC-H reused by read primitives.
